captions.linkedin:
4 trading days a month earned ALL the gains in the DJIA. For 90 years.

That's the Lakonishok-Smidt result, published in the Review of Financial Studies in 1988. Xu & McConnell re-tested it in the Financial Analysts Journal in 2006 and confirmed: virtually all excess return concentrated in a 4-day window.

The window: last trading day of the month plus the first 3 trading days of the next month.

The rest of the month? Cash performance.

The mechanic:

🔹 LONG EQUITY (index ETF or futures) at the close of the second-to-last trading day of the month
🔹 EXIT at the close of trading day +3 of the new month
🔹 FLAT THE REST OF THE MONTH (in cash or T-bills)
🔹 NO INDICATORS, NO SIGNALS, just exchange calendar dates
🔹 ~20% of trading days in market

Hypothesized driver: institutional cash flows. Pensions get contributions at month-end, payroll inflows hit retirement accounts, fund managers rebalance for month-end reporting. Net buying pressure concentrates in that window.

Documented across international developed markets, not just the US.

The lesson: you don't need to be in the market every day. You need to be in the right 4 days.

Strategy shared free. Performance depends on execution, sizing, and risk gates, that's the part we engineer.
